relevance_reason: Reports the first recessive (homozygous) NEFL mutation, E210X, in a consanguineous Palestinian family. The affected children had a severe, early-onset neuropathy with conduction velocities in the demyelinating range. The paper includes clinical, electrophysiological, nerve biopsy and functional data.

findings.statement: Yum et al. (2009) described 4 of 5 children of consanguineous Palestinian parents (first cousins) with a severe, progressive neuropathy. Onset was at about 1.5 years. All 4 had hypotonia in infancy and early childhood, mildly delayed motor milestones, slowly progressive distal atrophy and weakness of the feet and hands, and bilateral pes cavus. They also had moderate glove-and-stocking sensory impairment and absent ankle jerks. The oldest sib (23 years) used a walker and had proximal leg weakness and a waddling gait; the others walked with ankle-foot orthoses. CMT neuropathy scores were 16 to 27. None had enlarged nerves, pathologic reflexes, cranial neuropathies, or clinically evident hearing loss.
quotes: affecting 4 of 5 children of consanguineous parents (first cousins). The index patient (II-4) presented at age 2 years with toe walking

All 4 affected individuals had hypotonia during infancy and early childhood, mildly delayed motor milestones, slowly progressive atrophy and weakness in distal muscles of the feet and hands, and bilateral pes cavus.
None of them have ever had pathological reflexes, palpably enlarged nerves, ulcerated feet, cranial neuropathies, or clinically evident hearing loss.

findings.statement: Yum et al. (2009) found that in the affected sibs, sensory responses were absent or nearly so. Median and ulnar motor conduction velocities were severely slowed (12 to 25 m/s), and amplitudes became progressively smaller with age. Peroneal and tibial responses eventually became unobtainable, and EMG showed severe distal denervation. Visual evoked responses were prolonged in 3 of 4 affected children, indicating subclinical CNS axonal involvement; brain MRI was normal in the 3 who were tested.
quotes: The median and ulnar motor responses were severely slowed, ranging from 12 to 25 m/s, and had progressively smaller amplitudes with age.
Visual evoked responses (VERs) were done in 2008, and were prolonged in three of four affected children (Table 1).
Finally, the finding that 3 of 4 affected children have prolonged VERs indicates that there is subclinical involvement of the myelinated axons in the CNS.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased amplitude of sensory action potentials

phenotypes.text: reduced compound motor action potential amplitudes
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased compound muscle action potential amplitude

findings.statement: In the 4 affected sibs, Yum et al. (2009) found a homozygous c.628G>T transversion in the NEFL gene, which predicts a glu210-to-ter (E210X) substitution. Both parents were heterozygous carriers and the unaffected sib did not carry the mutation. The mutation was absent from more than 11,000 individuals analyzed at Athena Diagnostics. Sequencing of PMP22, GJB1, MPZ, EGR2, PRX, LMNA, GDAP1 and MFN2 found no other mutations. The authors stated that this was the first reported recessive NEFL mutation.
quotes: At position 628 in the cDNA (c.628), a homozygous G>T transversion was detected (c.628G>T), predicted to result in a glutamate>AMBER change at position 210 (E210X), in all four affected children. Both parents were heterozygous for this mutation, and their unaffected child did not harbor it (Fig. 1).
The E210X mutation has not been found in more than 11,000 individuals analyzed at Athena Diagnostics

findings.statement: Yum et al. (2009) examined a sural nerve biopsy from the index patient at age 16 years. Myelinated axon density was markedly reduced (1,300/mm vs about 6,000/mm in controls), and all myelinated axons were smaller than 3 microns and often irregular in shape. There were occasional regenerating clusters but no actively degenerating axons. Myelinated axons contained microtubules but no intermediate filaments. The axons were immunoreactive with an N-terminal NFL antiserum but not a C-terminal one, consistent with the presence of the truncated protein; NFM, NFH, peripherin and alpha-internexin were also detected.
quotes: the density of myelinated axons was 1300/mm, compared to ∼6000/ mm in normal controls. All myelinated axons were less than 3 microns in diameter
Myelinated axons had microtubules, but intermediate filaments were not present (Fig. 4C and Supplemental Fig. 5).
an antiserum against the C-terminus of NFL (which was predicted to be absent in the E210X mutant protein), did not label the axons.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased number of peripheral myelinated nerve fibers
Abnormal peripheral nerve morphology by anatomical site

findings.statement: In SW-13 vim- cells, Yum et al. (2009) found that the E210X mutant NFL did not form filaments, appeared diffuse and mostly nuclear, and accumulated poorly (a ~30-kDa band). It did not interfere with filament formation by coexpressed wildtype NFL or with the vimentin network, unlike the dominant Q333P mutant. The authors concluded that E210X causes a simple loss of function.
quotes: As shown in Fig. 5, the E210X mutant did not form filaments, but was typically found in a diffuse pattern, largely in the nucleus, with occasional cytoplasmic puncta in cells with higher levels of expression.
cells co-expressing WT NFL and E210X mutant formed filaments comparably to cells co-expressing WT NFL and an empty vector
Thus, at least in these assays, the E210X mutant does not have a dominant effect.

findings.statement: Yum et al. (2009) noted that the conduction velocities (about 20 m/s) fell in the demyelinating range. Because NEFL is not prominently expressed by myelinating Schwann cells, they concluded that the absence of large myelinated axons, which lack neurofilaments and fail to reach normal caliber, is the likely explanation for the slowed conduction. They suggested that neurofilaments are required to maintain myelinated PNS axons.
quotes: According to the conventional criterion that is used to separated demyelinating from axonal neuropathies, 38 m/s, their neuropathy would be classified as “demyelinating”.
the histological analysis of the biopsy indicates that the absence of large, myelinated axons is the likely explanation for the slowed conduction.

findings.statement: Yum et al. (2009) proposed the term 'severe, early-onset axonal neuropathy' (SEOAN) for the disorder in their patients. They noted resemblance to Dejerine-Sottas neuropathy but with faster conduction and distinct biopsy findings, and suggested the patients would be designated CMT2B5 under the OMIM scheme for recessive axonal neuropathies.
quotes: we find the term “severe, early-onset axonal neuropathy” (SEOAN) is a more fitting name for their neuropathy, but we emphasize that homozygous NEFL mutations should also be considered in evaluation of children with Déjérine-Sottas neuropathy.
our patients should be called CMT2B5

relevance_reason: Reports NEFL mutations, including the first homozygous nonsense mutation, in Japanese patients with CMT, some with the demyelinating form. Only the abstract was available.

findings.statement: Abe et al. (2009) screened the NEFL gene in 223 Japanese patients with CMT who were negative for mutations in other known CMT genes (PMP22, MPZ, GJB1, LITAF, EGR2, GDAP1, MTMR2 and PRX in the demyelinating form; MFN2, MPZ, GJB1, HSP27, HSP22 and GARS in the axonal form). They found 4 heterozygous NEFL missense mutations (pro8 to leu, glu90 to lys, asn98 to ser, and glu396 to lys) in 5 unrelated patients.
quotes: We investigated NEFL in 223 Japanese CMT patients who were negative for PMP22, MPZ, GJB1, LITAF, EGR2, GDAP1, MTMR2 and PRX in the demyelinating form
We detected four heterozygous missense mutations--Pro8Leu, Glu90Lys, Asn98Ser and Glu396Lys--in five unrelated patients

findings.statement: In 1 Japanese patient with CMT, Abe et al. (2009) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in the NEFL gene (glu140 to ter; E140X). They described this as the first report of a homozygous nonsense NEFL mutation.
quotes: a homozygous nonsense mutation, Glu140Stop, in one other patient
This is the first report of a homozygous nonsense mutation of NEFL.

findings.statement: Abe et al. (2009) reported that all 6 patients with NEFL mutations had mildly to moderately slowed nerve conduction velocities. They suggested that the slowing might be caused by a loss of large-diameter fibers.
quotes: All patients had mildly to moderately delayed nerve conduction velocities, possibly caused by a loss of large diameter fibers.

phenotypes.text: mildly to moderately delayed nerve conduction velocities

findings.statement: Abe et al. (2009) concluded that nonsense NEFL mutations probably cause a recessive phenotype, whereas missense mutations cause a dominant phenotype.
quotes: Results of our study show that nonsense NEFL mutations probably cause a recessive phenotype, in contrast to missense mutations, which cause a dominant phenotype.

relevance_reason: Reports NEFL mutations in CMT patients with early onset, severe phenotype and slowed nerve conduction velocities (demyelinating-range), the basis for CMT1F.

findings.statement: Jordanova et al. (2003) screened 323 patients with CMT or related peripheral neuropathies for mutations in the NEFL gene and identified 6 disease-associated missense mutations and one 3-bp in-frame deletion clustered in functionally defined domains of the NEFL protein. They suggested that NEFL mutations should be considered in the molecular evaluation of patients with sporadic or dominantly inherited CMT.
quotes: we screened 323 patients with CMT or related peripheral neuropathies
We detected six disease associated missense mutations and one 3-bp in-frame deletion clustered in functionally defined domains of the NEFL protein.
we also suggest that NEFL mutations need to be considered in the molecular evaluation of patients with sporadic or dominantly inherited CMT

findings.statement: Jordanova et al. (2003) found that patients with NEFL mutations had early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype, with moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities on electrophysiologic examination.
quotes: Patients have an early onset and often a severe clinical phenotype.
Electrophysiological examination shows moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities.

phenotypes.text: moderately to severely slowed nerve conduction velocities

findings.statement: Jordanova et al. (2003) reported the first nerve biopsy of a CMT patient with a de novo missense mutation in NEFL, which showed axonal pathology with axonal regeneration clusters and onion bulb formations.
quotes: We report the first nerve biopsy of a CMT patient with a de novo missense mutation in NEFL, and found an axonal pathology with axonal regeneration clusters and onion bulb formations.

variants.as_reported: de novo missense mutation in NEFL
